info.description: # starlette-compress [![PyPI - Python Version](https://shields.monicz.dev/pypi/pyversions/starlette-compress)](https://pypi.org/p/starlette-compress) **starlette-compress** compresses ASGI HTTP responses with Zstandard, Brotli, or Gzip. Use it with [Starlette](https://www.starlette.io), FastAPI, or another ASGI application on Python 3.11+. Works with asyncio and Trio, including streaming responses and server-sent events. ## Installation ```sh pip install starlette-compress ``` ## Add the middleware ### Starlette ```py from starlette.applications import Starlette from starlette.middleware import Middleware from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse from starlette.routing import Route from starlette_compress import CompressMiddleware async def homepage(request): return PlainTextResponse("Hello!" * 200) app = Starlette( routes=[Route("/", homepage)], middleware=[Middleware(CompressMiddleware)], ) ``` Serve `app` with your ASGI server. Responses are compressed according to the client's `Accept-Encoding` header. ### FastAPI ```py from fastapi import FastAPI from starlette_compress import CompressMiddleware app = FastAPI() app.add_middleware(CompressMiddleware) @app.get("/") async def homepage(): return {"message": "Hello!" * 200} ``` ## Configure compression ### Changing minimum response size `minimum_size` applies to an ordinary one-shot body: a terminal first body message below the threshold is forwarded unchanged. Once an ordinary response sends `more_body=True`, compression begins without buffering to reach the threshold, even if the entire response is small. Streaming-registered types (e.g. `text/event-stream`) bypass the threshold for one-shot bodies too. See the [constructor reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zaczero/pkgs/starlette-compress/2.0.0/starlette-compress/starlette_compress/__init__.py) for defaults. ```py from starlette.applications import Starlette from starlette.middleware import Middleware from starlette_compress import CompressMiddleware middleware = [ Middleware(CompressMiddleware, minimum_size=1000) ] app = Starlette(middleware=middleware) ``` ### Tuning compression levels Adjust compression levels to trade compression work for output size. Supported levels and defaults are in the [constructor reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zaczero/pkgs/starlette-compress/2.0.0/starlette-compress/starlette_compress/__init__.py). Enabled Brotli qualities and Gzip levels outside their documented ranges raise `ValueError` when the middleware is constructed. ```py from starlette.applications import Starlette from starlette.middleware import Middleware from starlette_compress import CompressMiddleware middleware = [ Middleware(CompressMiddleware, zstd_level=6, brotli_quality=6, gzip_level=6) ] app = Starlette(middleware=middleware) ``` ### Supporting custom content types Unknown content types are not compressed. Add or remove types before serving requests; see the [default media types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zaczero/pkgs/starlette-compress/2.0.0/starlette-compress/starlette_compress/_utils.py). ```py from starlette_compress import add_compress_type, remove_compress_type add_compress_type("application/my-custom-type") remove_compress_type("application/json") ``` ### Server-sent events (SSE) `text/event-stream` responses are compressed by default and bypass `minimum_size`. The compressor flushes after each non-empty continuing ASGI body message and finishes on the terminal message. It does not parse SSE frames: two events in one message share one flush, and empty continuation messages are skipped. The middleware forwards `http.response.start` immediately so clients such as `EventSource` can open before the first event, though the ASGI server may buffer it until the first body. On pathsend-capable scopes, start is deferred to the first body or pathsend message so a file send is never advertised as compressed. To opt out: ```py from starlette_compress import remove_compress_type remove_compress_type("text/event-stream") ``` NDJSON / JSONL are not registered by default. Opt in for compressed, incremental line delivery: ```py from starlette_compress import add_compress_type add_compress_type("application/x-ndjson", streaming=True) add_compress_type("application/jsonl", streaming=True) ``` Flushing makes compressed bytes available from the codec; proxy and CDN buffering remain separate. ### Dropping Accept-Encoding header By default, starlette-compress leaves the request `Accept-Encoding` header intact. Set `remove_accept_encoding=True` to remove it before calling downstream middleware/application. ## Response behavior Enabled algorithms are selected in server priority order: Zstandard, Brotli, then Gzip. A positive `q` makes a coding eligible; relative quality values do not reorder that priority. For example, `zstd;q=0.1, gzip;q=1` selects Zstandard. Non-positive or unparseable `q` values exclude a coding; `*` enables supported codings except explicit exclusions. Multiple `Accept-Encoding` fields are combined. No header, no eligible enabled coding, or `identity` alone uses the identity path. This middleware falls back to identity rather than returning 406 when no enabled coding is eligible. Only registered media types are eligible (parameters and case are ignored). Missing or unknown types, informational responses, status 204/205/304, `Content-Range`, and an existing non-identity `Content-Encoding` bypass compression. A delayed-start response whose first body is terminal gets its encoded `Content-Length`; streaming paths remove it. Eligible body responses merge `Accept-Encoding` into `Vary`, including the identity path, except ordinary bodies below threshold. Raw pathsend forwarding preserves the original headers. Ordinary streams have no per-message flush guarantee; register a type as [streaming](#server-sent-events-sse) for incremental delivery. Omitted `more_body` means false. Configure the process-wide registry before serving requests. Registration is case-insensitive and idempotent; a plain re-add retains streaming membership, and removal clears both memberships. `http.response.pathsend` is forwarded uncompressed when it is the first content message. The identity path preserves zero-copy capability; an encoded path removes `http.response.zerocopysend` from the downstream scope so raw file bytes cannot be appended to an encoded response. Middleware instances can be shared across event-loop threads. Codec errors propagate to the application/server. ## Reference and Support The [middleware reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zaczero/pkgs/starlette-compress/2.0.0/starlette-compress/starlette_compress/__init__.py) lists defaults and compression-level ranges. The [`add_compress_type` and `remove_compress_type` reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Zaczero/pkgs/starlette-compress/2.0.0/starlette-compress/starlette_compress/_utils.py) describes registry operations and default media types.
